sentences.zh: }}晉惠帝元康二年二月，天西北大裂。

translations.literal: In the second year of Yuankang of Emperor Hui of Jin, in the second month, the sky split open greatly in the northwest.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Yuankang (292 CE), during the reign of Emperor Hui of Jin, the northwestern sky rent apart in the second month.

translations.literal: According to Liu Xiang's interpretation: "When the sky splits, yang is insufficient;
translations.idiomatic: Liu Xiang explained the omen thus: "A rent in the heavens means yang is deficient;

translations.literal: when the earth quakes, yin is excessive."
translations.idiomatic: earthquakes mean yin is in surplus."

translations.literal: At that time the ruler remained silent and passive, while the empress dominated government.
translations.idiomatic: At the time the emperor sat in silence and left affairs to others, while the empress held sole power.

sentences.zh: 元康三年四月，熒惑守太微六十日。

translations.literal: In the fourth month of the third year of Yuankang, Mars stationed at Taiwei for sixty days.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month of the third year of Yuankang (293 CE), Mars lingered in the Taiwei asterism for sixty days.

sentences.zh: 占曰：「諸侯三公謀其上，必有斬臣。

translations.literal: The prognostication reads: "Feudal lords and the three dukes plot against their sovereign; there will surely be executed ministers."
translations.idiomatic: The omen was read as follows: "Regional lords and the three highest ministers will plot against the throne, and ministers will be put to death."

translations.literal: Another reading: "The Son of Heaven will lose the state."
translations.idiomatic: A second interpretation: "The emperor will lose his realm."

translations.literal: That spring Venus had been stationed at Bi; by then it had been there more than a hundred days.
translations.idiomatic: That spring Venus had taken up station at the Bi asterism and, by this time, had remained there for more than a hundred days.

translations.literal: The prognostication reads: "There will be anxiety over urgent decrees."
translations.idiomatic: The omen signified alarm over sudden imperial orders.

translations.literal: Another reading: "The chancellor will perish."
translations.idiomatic: Another reading: "The chief minister will die."

translations.literal: It also portends unrest on the borders.
translations.idiomatic: It also foretold turmoil along the frontier.

sentences.zh: 」是年，鎮、歲、太白三星聚于畢昴。

translations.literal: That year Saturn, Jupiter, and Venus gathered at Bi and Mao.
translations.idiomatic: That same year Saturn, Jupiter, and Venus converged in the Bi and Mao asterisms.

translations.literal: The prognostication reads: "This portends war and mourning."
translations.idiomatic: The reading was: "War and funerals will follow."

translations.literal: Bi and Mao correspond to the territory of Zhao.
translations.idiomatic: Bi and Mao are the celestial correlates of the Zhao region.

sentences.zh: 」後賈后陷殺太子，趙王廢后，又殺之，斬張華、裴頠，遂篡位，廢帝為太上皇。

translations.literal: Later Empress Jia entrapped and killed the crown prince; the Prince of Zhao deposed the empress and killed her as well, beheaded Zhang Hua and Pei Wei, then usurped the throne and demoted the emperor to Retired Emperor.
translations.idiomatic: In the sequel Empress Jia framed and murdered the heir apparent; the Prince of Zhao deposed and killed her, executed Zhang Hua and Pei Wei, seized the throne, and reduced Emperor Hui to a retired sovereign.

translations.literal: From then on the realm fell into continuous turmoil and calamity.
translations.idiomatic: From that point the empire entered an unbroken chain of rebellion and disaster.

sentences.zh: 元康五年四月，有星孛于奎，至軒轅、太微，經三台、大陵。

translations.literal: In the fourth month of the fifth year of Yuankang, a broom star appeared at Kui and passed through Xuanyuan and Taiwei, traversing the Three Terraces and Great Mound.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month of the fifth year of Yuankang (295 CE), a comet blazed at Kui and swept on through Xuanyuan and Taiwei, crossing the Three Terraces and Great Mound asterisms.

sentences.zh: 占曰：「奎為魯，又為庫兵，軒轅為後宮，太微天子廷，三台為三司，大陵有積屍死喪之事。

translations.literal: The prognostication reads: "Kui stands for Lu and also for the armory; Xuanyuan stands for the inner palace; Taiwei is the Son of Heaven's court; the Three Terraces stand for the three ministers; Great Mound portends heaped corpses and death and mourning."
translations.idiomatic: The omen was interpreted thus: "Kui corresponds to Lu and to the weapons storehouse; Xuanyuan to the harem; Taiwei to the imperial court; the Three Terraces to the three chief ministers; and Great Mound to mass death and mourning."

translations.literal: The next year the armory caught fire and the Western Qiang rebelled.
translations.idiomatic: The following year the imperial arsenal burned, and the Western Qiang rose in revolt.

sentences.zh: 後五年，司空張華遇禍，賈后廢死，魯公賈謐誅。

translations.literal: Five years later Minister of Works Zhang Hua met disaster, Empress Jia was deposed and put to death, and Duke of Lu Jia Mi was executed.
translations.idiomatic: Five years on, Zhang Hua as Minister of Works was destroyed, Empress Jia was deposed and killed, and Jia Mi, Duke of Lu, was put to death.

translations.literal: The year after that the Prince of Zhao, Lun, usurped the throne.
translations.idiomatic: Yet another year on, the Prince of Zhao, Sima Lun, seized the throne.

sentences.zh: 於是三王興兵討倫，士民戰死十餘萬人。

translations.literal: Thereupon the three princes raised armies to punish Lun, and more than a hundred thousand soldiers and civilians died in battle.
translations.idiomatic: The three princes then took the field against Lun, and well over a hundred thousand fighting men and common people perished in the fighting.

sentences.zh: 元康六年六月丙午夜，有枉矢自斗魁東南行。

translations.literal: At midnight on bingwu day in the sixth month of the sixth year of Yuankang, a Crooked Arrow star issued from the Dipper's head and traveled southeast.
translations.idiomatic: At midnight on a bingwu day in the sixth month of the sixth year of Yuankang (296 CE), a Crooked Arrow comet shot out from the head of the Northern Dipper and ran southeast.

translations.literal: According to the prognostication: "Chaos will strike down chaos."
translations.idiomatic: The reading given was: "Rebellion will destroy rebellion."

sentences.zh: 北斗主執殺，出斗魁，居中執殺者不直象也。

translations.literal: The Northern Dipper governs execution; when the star emerges from the Dipper's head, it is an image of the executioner at the center who is not upright.
translations.idiomatic: The Northern Dipper presides over executions; a star issuing from its head signifies a killer at the heart of power who lacks legitimacy.

translations.literal: In the tenth month Venus was visible in daylight.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month Venus appeared in broad daylight.

sentences.zh: 後趙王殺張、裴，廢賈后，以理太子之寃，因自篡盜，以至屠滅。

translations.literal: Later the Prince of Zhao killed Zhang and Pei, deposed Empress Jia, and claimed to redress the crown prince's wrong; then he himself usurped and plundered until he was slaughtered and destroyed.
translations.idiomatic: Afterward the Prince of Zhao executed Zhang and Pei, deposed Empress Jia under the pretext of avenging the heir apparent, then usurped power himself and was annihilated in the bloodshed that followed.

sentences.zh: 以亂伐亂，兵喪臣強之應也。

translations.literal: Chaos striking down chaos was the fulfillment of the portent of war, mourning, and powerful ministers.
translations.idiomatic: Rebellion consuming rebellion fulfilled the omen of war, slaughter, and ministers grown too strong.

sentences.zh: 元康九年二月，熒惑守心。

translations.literal: In the second month of the ninth year of Yuankang, Mars stationed at Antares.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month of the ninth year of Yuankang (299 CE), Mars lingered at Antares in the Heart asterism.

translations.literal: The prognostication reads: "The king finds it ominous."
translations.idiomatic: The omen was read as ill fortune for the sovereign.

translations.literal: In the eighth month Mars entered the Feathered Forest guard constellation.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month Mars entered the Feathered Forest, the asterism of the imperial guard.

translations.literal: The prognostication reads: "The palace guard will rise in great numbers."
translations.idiomatic: The reading was: "The palace armies will mobilize on a vast scale."

sentences.zh: 」後二年，惠帝見廢為太上皇，俄而三王起兵討倫，倫悉遣中軍兵，相距累月。

translations.literal: Two years later Emperor Hui was deposed as Retired Emperor; soon the three princes raised armies against Lun, and Lun sent out all his central army troops, and the two sides faced each other for many months.
translations.idiomatic: Two years on, Emperor Hui was reduced to retired emperor; before long the three princes marched against Lun, who committed his entire central army to the field, and the armies stood opposed for months on end.

sentences.zh: 晉惠帝永康元年三月，妖星見南方，中台星坼，太白晝見。

translations.literal: In the third month of the first year of Yongkang of Emperor Hui of Jin, an aberrant star appeared in the south, the Central Terrace star split, and Venus was visible in daylight.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month of the first year of Yongkang (300 CE), an ominous star showed in the south, the Central Terrace star fractured, and Venus shone by day.

sentences.zh: 占曰：「妖星出，天下大兵將起。

translations.literal: The prognostication reads: "When an aberrant star appears, great armies will rise throughout the realm."
translations.idiomatic: The omen signified that when a malign star appeared, empire-wide war would soon break out.

translations.literal: When the Terrace stars behave abnormally, the three dukes are troubled.
translations.idiomatic: An irregularity in the Terrace stars portended distress for the three highest ministers.

translations.literal: Venus visible in daylight portends disloyal ministers.
translations.idiomatic: Venus shining by day foretold treacherous subjects.

sentences.zh: 」是月，賈后殺太子，趙王倫尋廢殺后及司空張華，又廢帝自立。

translations.literal: That month Empress Jia killed the crown prince; soon the Prince of Zhao Lun deposed and killed the empress and Minister of Works Zhang Hua, then deposed the emperor and enthroned himself.
translations.idiomatic: That same month Empress Jia murdered the heir apparent; before long the Prince of Zhao deposed and killed her along with Zhang Hua as Minister of Works, then set aside the emperor and declared himself ruler.

sentences.zh: 於是三王並起，迭總大權。

translations.literal: Thereupon the three princes all rose up and in turn held supreme power.
translations.idiomatic: The three princes then rose together, each in turn seizing paramount authority.

sentences.zh: 永康元年五月，熒惑入南斗。

translations.literal: In the fifth month of the first year of Yongkang, Mars entered the Southern Dipper.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month of Yongkang 1, Mars entered the Southern Dipper.

translations.literal: The prognostication reads: "The chief minister will die and armies will rise on a great scale."
translations.idiomatic: The omen read: "The chief minister will perish and war will erupt on a vast scale."

translations.literal: The Dipper also corresponds to the Wu region.
translations.idiomatic: The Dipper is also the celestial correlate of Wu.

sentences.zh: 」是時趙王倫為相，明年篡位，三王興師誅之。

translations.literal: At that time the Prince of Zhao Lun was chancellor; the next year he usurped the throne, and the three princes raised armies to execute him.
translations.idiomatic: At the time the Prince of Zhao served as chief minister; the following year he seized the throne, and the three princes took the field to destroy him.

translations.literal: In the second year of Taian, Shi Bing captured Yangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Taian (302 CE), Shi Bing overran Yangzhou.

sentences.zh: 永康元年八月，熒惑入箕。

translations.literal: In the eighth month of the first year of Yongkang, Mars entered the Winnowing Basket.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month of Yongkang 1, Mars entered the Winnowing Basket asterism.

translations.literal: The prognostication reads: "The ruler loses his position and armies rise."
translations.idiomatic: The reading was: "The sovereign will lose his throne and war will break out."

sentences.zh: 」十二月，彗出牽牛之西，指天市。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month a comet appeared west of the Lead Ox and pointed toward the Celestial Market.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month a comet rose west of the Lead Ox and aimed toward the Celestial Market Enclosure.

sentences.zh: 占曰：「牛者七政始，彗出之，改元易號之象也。

translations.literal: The prognostication reads: "The Ox is where the seven regulators begin; when a comet emerges there, it is a sign of changing the era name and altering the reign title."
translations.idiomatic: The omen was read: "The Lead Ox marks the starting point of the seven regulators; a comet there portends a change of reign era and imperial title."

sentences.zh: 」天市一名天府，一名天子禖，帝座在其中。

translations.literal: The Celestial Market is also called the Heavenly Storehouse and the Son of Heaven's Spirit Tablet; the Imperial Seat lies within it.
translations.idiomatic: The Celestial Market is also known as the Heavenly Treasury and the Son of Heaven's Spirit Altar; the emperor's throne star sits within it.

sentences.zh: 明年，趙王篡位，改元，尋為大兵所滅。

translations.literal: The next year the Prince of Zhao usurped the throne and changed the era name; soon he was destroyed by great armies.
translations.idiomatic: The following year the Prince of Zhao seized power and proclaimed a new era; before long he was annihilated by the armies raised against him.

sentences.zh: 永康二年二月，太白出西方，逆行入東井。

translations.literal: In the second month of the second year of Yongkang, Venus emerged in the west, moved retrograde, and entered the Eastern Well.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month of Yongkang 2, Venus appeared in the west, turned retrograde, and entered the Eastern Well asterism.

translations.literal: The prognostication reads: "The state loses good government and ministers create disorder."
translations.idiomatic: The omen signified that the state would lose its proper governance and ministers would rise in rebellion.

translations.literal: In the fourth month a comet appeared in the Qi region of the sky.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month a comet showed in the celestial territory of Qi.

translations.literal: The prognostication reads: "Qi will suffer war and mourning."
translations.idiomatic: The reading was: "Qi will see war and death."

translations.literal: At that time the Prince of Qi, Jiong, raised an army to punish the Prince of Zhao, Lun.
translations.idiomatic: At the time the Prince of Qi, Sima Jiong, took the field against the Prince of Zhao, Sima Lun.

sentences.zh: 倫滅，冏擁兵不朝，專權淫奓，明年誅死。

translations.literal: When Lun was destroyed, Jiong held his army and did not attend court, monopolized power and grew extravagant and arrogant, and was executed the next year.
translations.idiomatic: After Lun's fall Jiong kept his troops and refused to come to court, seized sole authority and grew arrogant and dissolute, and was put to death the following year.

sentences.zh: 晉惠帝永寧元年，自正月至于閏月，五星互經天。

translations.literal: In the first year of Yongning of Emperor Hui of Jin, from the first month through the intercalary month, the five planets in turn crossed the meridian at noon.
translations.idiomatic: Throughout the first year of Yongning (301 CE), from the first month through the intercalary month, all five planets in succession crossed the sky at midday.

translations.literal: The tradition on stars says: "The sun is yang and represents the way of the ruler.
translations.idiomatic: Star lore holds that "the sun is yang and embodies the ruler's way;

translations.literal: Stars are yin and represent the way of ministers.
translations.idiomatic: the stars are yin and embody the minister's way.

sentences.zh: 日出則星亡，臣不得專也。

translations.literal: When the sun rises the stars vanish, and ministers may not act on their own authority."
translations.idiomatic: When the sun rises the stars disappear, and ministers must not seize independent power."

sentences.zh: 晝而星見午上者為經天，其占為不臣，為更王。

translations.literal: When stars are visible at noon above the meridian it is called crossing heaven; the prognostication is disloyal ministers and a change of kings.
translations.idiomatic: A star visible at noon on the meridian is said to cross heaven; the omen is treason and a change of ruler.

sentences.zh: 今五星悉經天，天變所未有也。

translations.literal: Now all five planets crossed heaven—a celestial change never before recorded.
translations.idiomatic: Now all five planets crossed the meridian by day—a heavenly anomaly without precedent.

sentences.zh: 」石氏說曰：「辰星晝見，其國不亡，則大亂。

translations.literal: The Shi clan interpretation says: "When Mercury is visible in daylight, if the state does not perish, there will be great chaos."
translations.idiomatic: The Shi school's reading held: "If Mercury appears by day, the realm will either fall or plunge into great disorder."

sentences.zh: 」是後台鼎方伯，互秉大權，二帝流亡，遂至六夷強，迭據華夏，亦載籍所未有也。

translations.literal: Afterward regional strongmen at the court and in the provinces in turn held supreme power; two emperors went into exile; and in the end the six barbarian peoples grew strong and in succession occupied the Central Realm—also something never before recorded in the annals.
translations.idiomatic: Afterward powerful ministers and regional lords seized power in turn; two emperors were driven into exile; and eventually the six non-Chinese peoples grew mighty and one after another held the heartland—again an event without parallel in the historical record.

sentences.zh: 永寧元年五月，太白晝見。

translations.literal: In the fifth month of the first year of Yongning, Venus was visible in daylight.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month of Yongning 1, Venus appeared in daylight.

translations.literal: The prognostication is the same as in the previous entry.
translations.idiomatic: The omen is interpreted as in the preceding passage.

translations.literal: In the seventh month Jupiter stationed at Emptiness and Rooftop.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month Jupiter lingered in the Emptiness and Rooftop asterisms.

translations.literal: The prognostication reads: "When Wood stations at Emptiness and Rooftop, there is anxiety over warfare."
translations.idiomatic: The omen read: "Jupiter at Emptiness and Rooftop portends the threat of war."

translations.literal: Another reading: "Stationing at Emptiness means famine;
translations.idiomatic: Another reading: "Lingering at Emptiness means famine;

translations.literal: stationing at Rooftop means corvée labor is burdensome and the lower orders are exhausted and depleted."
translations.idiomatic: at Rooftop means corvée burdens grow heavy and the common people are driven to exhaustion."

translations.literal: Mercury entered Taiwei.
translations.idiomatic: Mercury entered the Taiwei Enclosure.

translations.literal: The prognostication reads: "This portends internal disorder."
translations.idiomatic: The omen signified civil strife within the court.

translations.literal: Another reading: "Ministers will kill one another."
translations.idiomatic: Another reading: "The ministers will slaughter one another."

translations.literal: Venus stationed at the Right Rear Gate.
translations.idiomatic: Venus lingered at the Right Rear Gate of the palace enclosure.

translations.literal: The prognostication reads: "This portends armies, disorder, and rebels."
translations.idiomatic: The reading was: "War, rebellion, and treachery will follow."

sentences.zh: 」八月戊午，鎮星犯左執法，又犯上相。

translations.literal: On wuwu day in the eighth month Saturn encroached on the Left Law Enforcer and also encroached on the Upper Minister.
translations.idiomatic: On a wuwu day in the eighth month Saturn trespassed against the Left Law Enforcer star and then against the Upper Minister star.

translations.literal: The prognostication reads: "The upper minister is troubled."
translations.idiomatic: The omen portended calamity for the chief minister.

translations.literal: Mars stationed at the Hairy Head.
translations.idiomatic: Mars lingered in the Hairy Head asterism.

translations.literal: The prognostication reads: "Zhao and Wei will suffer disaster."
translations.idiomatic: The reading was: "Disaster will strike the Zhao and Wei regions."

translations.literal: Mercury stationed at the Carriage Ghost.
translations.idiomatic: Mercury lingered at the Carriage Ghost asterism.

translations.literal: The prognostication reads: "Qin will suffer disaster."
translations.idiomatic: The omen signified disaster for the Qin region.

translations.literal: On dingwei day in the ninth month the moon encroached on the Left Horn.
translations.idiomatic: On a dingwei day in the ninth month the moon trespassed against the Left Horn star.

translations.literal: The prognostication reads: "The ruler is troubled."
translations.idiomatic: The reading was: "The sovereign will face grave anxiety."

translations.literal: Another reading: "The Left General will die and armies will rise throughout the realm."
translations.idiomatic: Another reading: "The Left General will perish and war will spread across the empire."

sentences.zh: 二年四月癸酉，歲星晝見。

translations.literal: On guiyou day in the fourth month of the second year, Jupiter was visible in daylight.
translations.idiomatic: On a guiyou day in the fourth month of the second year, Jupiter shone by day.

translations.literal: The prognostication reads: "This portends powerful ministers."
translations.idiomatic: The omen signified that ministers had grown too strong.

translations.literal: In the tenth month Mars and Venus contended at Emptiness and Rooftop.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month Mars and Venus clashed in the Emptiness and Rooftop asterisms.

translations.literal: The prognostication reads: "Great armies will rise; armies will be broken and generals killed."
translations.idiomatic: The omen read: "War on a vast scale will erupt; armies will be shattered and commanders slain."

translations.literal: Emptiness and Rooftop also correspond to the Qi region.
translations.idiomatic: Emptiness and Rooftop are also the celestial correlates of Qi.

translations.literal: In the twelfth month Mars assaulted Venus at the Encampment.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month Mars struck at Venus in the Encampment asterism.

sentences.zh: 占曰：「天下兵起，亡君之戒。

translations.literal: The prognostication reads: "Armies will rise throughout the realm; this is a warning of the ruler's destruction."
translations.idiomatic: The reading was: "Empire-wide war will break out—a warning that the sovereign may be lost."

translations.literal: Another reading: "The chancellor will be replaced."
translations.idiomatic: Another reading: "The chief minister will be changed."

sentences.zh: 」初齊王冏定京都，因留輔政，遂專慠無君。

translations.literal: At first the Prince of Qi Jiong secured the capital and therefore remained to assist in government, but then he monopolized power arrogantly and acted as though there were no ruler.
translations.idiomatic: At first the Prince of Qi, having pacified the capital, stayed on as regent; he then seized sole authority and behaved with arrogant disregard for the throne.

sentences.zh: 是月，成都、河間檄長沙王乂討之。

translations.literal: That month the princes of Chengdu and Hejian issued proclamations urging the Prince of Changsha, Ai, to campaign against him.
translations.idiomatic: That month the princes of Chengdu and Hejian issued calls to arms summoning the Prince of Changsha, Sima Ai, to march against him.

translations.literal: Jiong and Ai fought one another, attacking and burning the palace halls.
translations.idiomatic: Jiong and Ai battled each other, assaulting and setting fire to the palace compounds.

sentences.zh: 冏兵敗夷滅，又殺其兄上軍將軍寔以下二十餘人。

translations.literal: Jiong's army was defeated and he was destroyed; more than twenty of his kin were also killed, including his elder brother Shangjun General Shi and those below him.
translations.idiomatic: Jiong's forces were crushed and he was annihilated; more than twenty of his family followed him to death, including his elder brother Shi as General of the Upper Army.

sentences.zh: 太安二年，成都攻長沙，於是公私飢困，百姓力屈。

translations.literal: In the second year of Taian the Prince of Chengdu attacked the Prince of Changsha; public and private stores alike suffered famine, and the common people were exhausted.
translations.idiomatic: In Taian 2 the Prince of Chengdu attacked the Prince of Changsha; famine gripped public granaries and private households alike, and the people were driven past endurance.

sentences.zh: 晉惠帝太安二年二月，太白入昴。

translations.literal: In the second month of the second year of Taian of Emperor Hui of Jin, Venus entered the Hairy Head.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month of Taian 2 (302 CE), during the reign of Emperor Hui of Jin, Venus entered the Hairy Head asterism.

translations.literal: The prognostication reads: "The realm will be disturbed and armies will rise on a great scale."
translations.idiomatic: The omen read: "The empire will fall into turmoil and war will erupt on a vast scale."

translations.literal: In the third month a comet appeared in the east, pointing toward the Three Terraces.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month a comet showed in the east, its tail aimed at the Three Terraces.

translations.literal: The prognostication reads: "An image of war and mourning."
translations.idiomatic: The omen read: "War and death."

translations.literal: The Three Terraces stand for the three dukes.
translations.idiomatic: The Three Terraces correspond to the three chief ministers.

translations.literal: In the seventh month Mars entered the Eastern Well.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month Mars entered the Eastern Well asterism.

translations.literal: The prognostication reads: "Armies will rise and the state will fall into disorder."
translations.idiomatic: The omen read: "War will break out and the realm will be thrown into chaos."

translations.literal: That autumn Venus stationed at the Senior General star in Taiwei.
translations.idiomatic: That autumn Venus lingered at the Senior General star in the Taiwei enclosure.

translations.literal: The prognostication reads: "The senior general will perish by arms."
translations.idiomatic: The reading was: "The senior general will die in battle."

translations.literal: That winter the princes of Chengdu and Hejian attacked Luoyang.
translations.idiomatic: That winter the princes of Chengdu and Hejian marched on Luoyang.

sentences.zh: 三年正月，東海王越執長沙王乂，張方又殺之。

translations.literal: In the first month of the third year the Prince of Donghai, Yue, seized the Prince of Changsha, Ai, and Zhang Fang then killed him.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of Taian 3 the Prince of Donghai, Sima Yue, seized the Prince of Changsha, Sima Ai, and Zhang Fang then put him to death.

sentences.zh: 太安二年八月，長沙王奉帝出距二王，庚午，舍于玄武館。

translations.literal: In the eighth month of the second year of Taian the Prince of Changsha escorted the emperor forth to resist the two princes; on gengwu day he lodged at the Black Tortoise Lodge.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month of Taian 2 the Prince of Changsha led the emperor out to oppose the two princes; on a gengwu day they halted at the Black Tortoise Lodge.

sentences.zh: 是日天中裂為二，有聲如雷。

translations.literal: That day the sky at the zenith split into two, and there was a sound like thunder.
translations.idiomatic: That day the sky at the meridian rent in two, with a thunderous roar.

sentences.zh: 三占同元康，臣下專僭之象也。

translations.literal: The three prognostications match Yuankang: an image of subordinates monopolizing power and overstepping their rank.
translations.idiomatic: All three readings matched those of Yuankang—an omen of subordinates seizing authority and acting above their station.

sentences.zh: 是時長沙王擅權，後成都、河間、東海又迭專威命，是其應也。

translations.literal: At that time the Prince of Changsha monopolized power; afterward the princes of Chengdu, Hejian, and Donghai in turn wielded sole authority—this was the fulfillment.
translations.idiomatic: At the time the Prince of Changsha held sole power; afterward the princes of Chengdu, Hejian, and Donghai each in turn commanded by their own authority—and so the omen was fulfilled.

sentences.zh: 太安二年十一月辛巳，有星晝隕中天，北下有聲如雷。

translations.literal: On xinsi day in the eleventh month of the second year of Taian a star fell in daylight at the zenith; to the north below there was a sound like thunder.
translations.idiomatic: On an xinsi day in the eleventh month of Taian 2 a star fell by day at the meridian, and to the north below came a thunderous crash.

sentences.zh: 桉占，「名曰營首，營首所在，下有大兵流血。

translations.literal: According to the prognostication: "It is called Camp Head; where Camp Head appears, below there will be great armies and flowing blood."
translations.idiomatic: The omen was read thus: "It is named Camp Head; wherever Camp Head appears, great armies below will shed blood."

sentences.zh: 」明年，劉淵、石勒攻略并州，多所殘滅。

translations.literal: The next year Liu Yuan and Shi Le raided and seized Bing Province, slaughtering on a vast scale.
translations.idiomatic: The following year Liu Yuan and Shi Le overran Bing Province, leaving widespread devastation in their wake.

sentences.zh: 王浚起燕、代，引鮮卑攻掠鄴中，百姓塗地。

translations.literal: Wang Jun rose in Yan and Dai, leading Xianbei in attacks and plunder against Ye; the common people were strewn dead upon the ground.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Jun raised forces in Yan and Dai and led Xianbei raids against Ye; the people were slaughtered until the land ran with blood.

translations.literal: A sound like thunder is an image of wrath.
translations.idiomatic: The thunderous sound signified celestial anger.

sentences.zh: 太安二年十一月庚辰，歲星入月中。

translations.literal: On gengchen day in the eleventh month of the second year of Taian Jupiter entered the moon.
translations.idiomatic: On a gengchen day in the eleventh month of Taian 2 Jupiter entered the moon.

translations.literal: The prognostication reads: "The state will drive out its chancellor."
translations.idiomatic: The omen read: "The state will expel its chief minister."

translations.literal: On renyin day in the twelfth month Venus encroached on the moon.
translations.idiomatic: On a renyin day in the twelfth month Venus crossed the moon.

translations.literal: The prognostication reads: "There will be warfare throughout the realm."
translations.idiomatic: The reading was: "War will engulf the empire."

sentences.zh: 」太安三年正月己卯，月犯太白，占同青龍。

translations.literal: On jimao day in the first month of the third year of Taian the moon encroached on Venus; the prognostication matches Qinglong.
translations.idiomatic: On a jimao day in the first month of Taian 3 the moon crossed Venus; the omen was read as in Qinglong.

translations.literal: Mars entered the Southern Dipper; the prognostication matches Yongkang.
translations.idiomatic: Mars entered the Southern Dipper; the reading matched that of Yongkang.

translations.literal: That month Mars again encroached on Jupiter.
translations.idiomatic: That same month Mars crossed Jupiter again.

translations.literal: The prognostication reads: "There will be a great battle."
translations.idiomatic: The omen read: "A great battle will follow."

sentences.zh: 」七月，左衞將軍陳眕率眾奉帝伐成都，六軍敗績，兵逼乘輿。

translations.literal: In the seventh month Left Guard General Chen Zhen led troops escorting the emperor to campaign against Chengdu; the six armies were routed and enemy forces pressed upon the imperial carriage.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month Left Guard General Chen Zhen marched with the emperor against the Prince of Chengdu; the imperial armies were crushed and rebel troops closed in on the sovereign's carriage.

sentences.zh: 九月，王浚又攻成都于鄴，鄴潰，成都王由是喪亡。

translations.literal: In the ninth month Wang Jun again attacked the Prince of Chengdu at Ye; Ye fell, and the Prince of Chengdu thereby perished.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month Wang Jun again assailed the Prince of Chengdu at Ye; the city fell, and the Prince of Chengdu was destroyed.

translations.literal: The emperor returned to Luoyang, but Zhang Fang coerced him to proceed to Chang'an.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor returned to Luoyang, only for Zhang Fang to force him onward to Chang'an.

sentences.zh: 是時天下盜賊羣起，張昌尤盛。

translations.literal: At that time bandits and robbers rose throughout the realm in swarms; Zhang Chang was especially powerful.
translations.idiomatic: At the time rebels and bandits rose everywhere; Zhang Chang's uprising was the fiercest of all.

translations.literal: Two years later Emperor Hui died.
translations.idiomatic: Two years later Emperor Hui passed away.

sentences.zh: 晉惠帝永興元年五月，客星守畢。

translations.literal: In the fifth month of the first year of Yongxing of Emperor Hui of Jin, a guest star stationed at the Net.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month of Yongxing 1, during the reign of Emperor Hui of Jin, a guest star lingered at the Net asterism.

translations.literal: The prognostication reads: "The Son of Heaven will have no heir."
translations.idiomatic: The omen read: "The emperor's line will end without succession."

translations.literal: Another reading: "Ministers will be executed."
translations.idiomatic: A second reading: "Ministers will be put to death."

sentences.zh: 」七月庚申，太白犯角、亢，經房、心，歷尾、箕。

translations.literal: On gengshen day in the seventh month Venus encroached on the Horn and Neck, passed through the Room and Heart, and traversed the Tail and Winnowing Basket.
translations.idiomatic: On a gengshen day in the seventh month Venus crossed the Horn and Neck, passed through the Room and Heart, and swept on through the Tail and Winnowing Basket.

translations.literal: In the ninth month it entered the Southern Dipper.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month it entered the Southern Dipper.

translations.literal: The prognostication reads: "Encroaching on the Horn—empire-wide war;
translations.idiomatic: The reading was: "Crossing the Horn foretells empire-wide war;

translations.literal: encroaching on the Neck—great armies, and the ruler will be anxious;
translations.idiomatic: crossing the Neck, great armies and anxiety for the sovereign;

translations.literal: entering the Room and Heart—war and mourning;
translations.idiomatic: entering the Room and Heart, war and death;

translations.literal: encroaching on the Tail—generals and common people will revolt;
translations.idiomatic: crossing the Tail, generals and commoners will rise in rebellion;

translations.literal: encroaching on the Winnowing Basket—the chief consort will be anxious.
translations.idiomatic: crossing the Winnowing Basket, distress for the empress.

translations.literal: Another reading: "The realm will fall into disorder."
translations.idiomatic: A second reading: "The empire will be thrown into chaos."

translations.literal: Entering the Southern Dipper—war and mourning.
translations.idiomatic: Entering the Southern Dipper brings war and death.

translations.literal: Another reading: "Generals will rebel."
translations.idiomatic: Another reading: "Generals will rise in revolt."

sentences.zh: 」其所犯守，又兗、豫、幽、冀、揚州之分也。

translations.literal: The regions it encroached upon and stationed over also correspond to Yan, Yu, You, Ji, and Yang provinces.
translations.idiomatic: The asterisms it crossed and lingered in also mapped to Yan, Yu, You, Ji, and Yang provinces.

translations.literal: That year in the seventh month there was the Battle of Dangyin.
translations.idiomatic: That year the Battle of Dangyin was fought in the seventh month.

sentences.zh: 九月，王浚殺幽州刺史和演，攻鄴，鄴潰。

translations.literal: In the ninth month Wang Jun killed You Province Inspector He Yan, attacked Ye, and Ye fell.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month Wang Jun killed You Province Inspector He Yan, assaulted Ye, and the city fell.

translations.literal: Thereupon Yan and Yu became the crossroads of warfare throughout the realm.
translations.idiomatic: Thereafter Yan and Yu became the main battlegrounds of the empire.

sentences.zh: 陳敏又亂揚土，劉淵、石勒、李雄等並起微賤，跨有州郡。

translations.literal: Chen Min also stirred rebellion in the Yang region; Liu Yuan, Shi Le, Li Xiong, and others all rose from humble origins and seized command of provinces and commanderies.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Min also raised rebellion in the Yang region; Liu Yuan, Shi Le, Li Xiong, and others all rose from humble origins to hold whole provinces and commanderies.

translations.literal: Empress Yang was repeatedly imprisoned and deposed.
translations.idiomatic: Empress Yang was repeatedly imprisoned and set aside.

sentences.zh: 光熙元年，惠帝崩，終無繼嗣。

translations.literal: In the first year of Guangxi Emperor Hui died, and in the end he had no successor.
translations.idiomatic: In Guangxi 1 Emperor Hui died, leaving no heir to the throne.

sentences.zh: 永興元年七月乙丑，星隕有聲。

translations.literal: On yichou day in the seventh month of the first year of Yongxing a star fell with a sound.
translations.idiomatic: On a yichou day in the seventh month of Yongxing 1 a star fell with an audible crash.

translations.literal: In the tenth month of the second year a star again fell with a sound.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month of the second year another star fell with a crash.

sentences.zh: 按劉向說，民去其土之象也。

translations.literal: According to Liu Xiang's interpretation, this is an image of the people leaving their native soil.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Xiang explained it as an omen of the people driven from their homeland.

translations.literal: Afterward the Central Lands were lost.
translations.idiomatic: Thereafter the heartland of China was lost.

sentences.zh: 永興元年十二月壬寅夜，赤氣亘天，砰隱有聲。

translations.literal: On the night of renyin day in the twelfth month of the first year of Yongxing red vapor stretched across the sky, with muffled rumbling sounds.
translations.idiomatic: On the night of a renyin day in the twelfth month of Yongxing 1 red vapor filled the sky, accompanied by muffled thunder.

sentences.zh: 二年十月丁丑，赤氣見在北方，東西竟天。

translations.literal: On dingchou day in the tenth month of the second year red vapor appeared in the north, stretching from east to west across the entire sky.
translations.idiomatic: On a dingchou day in the tenth month of the second year red vapor showed in the north, spanning the sky from east to west.

translations.literal: The prognostication reads: "Together they signify great armies."
translations.idiomatic: The omen read: "Together they foretold war on a vast scale."

translations.literal: Muffled rumbling sounds are an image of wrath.
translations.idiomatic: The muffled thunder signified celestial anger.

translations.literal: Afterward the four seas were clouded with turmoil and the nine domains exchanged arms.
translations.idiomatic: Thereafter turmoil spread across the four seas and war crossed every domain of the empire.

sentences.zh: 永興二年四月丙子，太白犯狼星。

translations.literal: On bingzi day in the fourth month of the second year of Yongxing Venus encroached on the Wolf Star.
translations.idiomatic: On a bingzi day in the fourth month of Yongxing 2 Venus crossed the Wolf Star.

translations.literal: The prognostication reads: "Great armies will rise."
translations.idiomatic: The omen read: "War will erupt on a great scale."

translations.literal: In the ninth month Jupiter stationed at the Eastern Well.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month Jupiter lingered at the Eastern Well asterism.

translations.literal: The prognostication reads: "There will be warfare."
translations.idiomatic: The reading was: "War will follow."

translations.literal: The Well also corresponds to the Qin region.
translations.idiomatic: The Well is also the celestial correlate of Qin.

sentences.zh: 」是年，苟晞破公師藩，張方破范陽王虓，關西諸將攻河間王顒，顒奔走，東海王迎殺之。

translations.literal: That year Gou Xi defeated Gongshi Fan; Zhang Fang defeated the Prince of Fanyang, Biao; the generals of Guanxi attacked the Prince of Hejian, Yong, who fled; and the Prince of Donghai intercepted and killed him.
translations.idiomatic: That year Gou Xi routed Gongshi Fan; Zhang Fang crushed the Prince of Fanyang, Sima Biao; the generals of Guanxi assailed the Prince of Hejian, Sima Yong, who fled; and the Prince of Donghai intercepted and killed him.

sentences.zh: 永興二年八月，星孛于昴、畢。

translations.literal: In the eighth month of the second year of Yongxing a broom star appeared at the Hairy Head and the Net.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month of Yongxing 2 a comet blazed at the Hairy Head and the Net.

translations.literal: The prognostication reads: "It portends war and mourning."
translations.idiomatic: The omen read: "War and death."

translations.literal: The Hairy Head and the Net also correspond to the Zhao and Wei regions.
translations.idiomatic: The Hairy Head and the Net are also the celestial correlates of Zhao and Wei.

sentences.zh: 十月丁丑，有星孛于北斗。

translations.literal: On dingchou day in the tenth month a broom star appeared at the Northern Dipper.
translations.idiomatic: On a dingchou day in the tenth month a comet appeared at the Northern Dipper.

sentences.zh: 占曰：「璿璣更授，天子出走。

translations.literal: The prognostication reads: "The jade pivot will be transferred anew; the Son of Heaven will flee."
translations.idiomatic: The omen read: "The celestial pivot will change hands; the emperor will flee the capital."

translations.literal: It also reads: "Powerful states will raise armies; feudal lords will contend for authority."
translations.idiomatic: It also read: "Strong states will take the field; regional lords will struggle for power."

translations.literal: Afterward all had their fulfillment.
translations.idiomatic: In every case the omens were fulfilled.

translations.literal: The next year Emperor Hui died.
translations.idiomatic: The following year Emperor Hui died.

sentences.zh: 晉惠帝光熙元年四月，太白失行，自翼入尾、箕。

translations.literal: In the fourth month of the first year of Guangxi of Emperor Hui of Jin, Venus lost its proper course, entering the Tail and Winnowing Basket from the Wings.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month of Guangxi 1, during the reign of Emperor Hui of Jin, Venus strayed from its path, passing from the Wings into the Tail and Winnowing Basket.

sentences.zh: 占曰：「太白失行而北，是謂返生。

translations.literal: The prognostication reads: "When Venus loses its course and turns north, this is called returning to life."
translations.idiomatic: The omen read: "When Venus strays northward from its path, it is called retrograde rebirth."

translations.literal: If there is not a shattered army, there will surely be a slaughtered city.
translations.idiomatic: If armies are not broken, cities will be put to the sword.

sentences.zh: 」五月，汲桑攻鄴，魏郡太守馮嵩出戰大敗，桑遂害東燕王騰，殺萬餘人，焚燒魏時宮室皆盡。

translations.literal: In the fifth month Ji Sang attacked Ye; Wei Commandery Administrator Feng Song went forth to battle and was routed; Sang then killed the Prince of Dongyan, Teng, slaughtered more than ten thousand people, and burned all the palace halls of Wei times to nothing.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month Ji Sang assaulted Ye; Wei Commandery Administrator Feng Song marched out and was crushed; Sang then killed the Prince of Dongyan, Sima Teng, put more than ten thousand people to death, and burned every palace hall left from Wei times to the ground.

sentences.zh: 光熙元年五月，枉矢西南流。

translations.literal: In the fifth month of the first year of Guangxi a Crooked Arrow star flowed southwest.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month of Guangxi 1 a Crooked Arrow comet streaked southwest.

translations.literal: The prognostication reads: "An image of using disorder to attack disorder."
translations.idiomatic: The omen read: "An image of rebellion consuming rebellion."

sentences.zh: 」是時司馬越西破河間，奉迎大駕。

translations.literal: At that time Sima Yue defeated Hejian in the west and escorted the imperial carriage in welcome.
translations.idiomatic: At the time Sima Yue crushed the Prince of Hejian in the west and escorted the emperor back to the capital.

sentences.zh: 尋收繆胤、何綏等，肆其無君之心，天下惡之。

translations.literal: Soon afterward he seized Miao Yin, He Sui, and others, giving free rein to his heart without a ruler; the realm despised him.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward he arrested Miao Yin, He Sui, and others, revealing his contempt for the throne; the empire turned against him.

sentences.zh: 死而石勒焚其屍柩，是其應也。

translations.literal: After his death Shi Le burned his coffin—this was the fulfillment.
translations.idiomatic: After his death Shi Le burned his coffin—and so the omen was fulfilled.

sentences.zh: 光熙元年九月丁未，熒惑守心。

translations.literal: On dingwei day in the ninth month of the first year of Guangxi Mars stationed at Antares.
translations.idiomatic: On a dingwei day in the ninth month of Guangxi 1 Mars lingered at Antares in the Heart asterism.

translations.literal: The prognostication reads: "The king will regard it as an evil omen."
translations.idiomatic: The omen read: "It bodes ill for the sovereign."

translations.literal: On jihai day Saturn stationed at the Room and Heart and again encroached on Jupiter.
translations.idiomatic: On a jihai day Saturn lingered in the Room and Heart and crossed Jupiter again.

translations.literal: The prognostication reads: "When Earth stations at the Room, there will be much calamity and mourning."
translations.idiomatic: The reading was: "When Saturn lingers in the Room, calamity and death will multiply."

translations.literal: Stationing at the Heart—internal disorder within the state and an empire-wide amnesty.
translations.idiomatic: Lingering at the Heart foretells civil strife within the realm and a general amnesty.

translations.literal: It also reads: "When Saturn and Jupiter conjoin, there is internal disorder."
translations.idiomatic: It also read: "When Saturn and Jupiter meet, civil war follows."

sentences.zh: 」是時司馬越秉權，終以無禮破滅，內亂之應也。

translations.literal: At that time Sima Yue held power; in the end he was destroyed for his lack of propriety—this was the fulfillment of internal disorder.
translations.idiomatic: At the time Sima Yue held sole power; he was ultimately destroyed for his insolence toward the throne—the omen of civil strife fulfilled.

sentences.zh: 十一月，惠帝崩，懷帝即位，大赦天下。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month Emperor Hui died; Emperor Huai ascended the throne and proclaimed a general amnesty throughout the realm.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month Emperor Hui died; Emperor Huai took the throne and granted a general amnesty.

sentences.zh: 光熙元年十二月癸未，太白犯填星。

translations.literal: On guiwei day in the twelfth month of the first year of Guangxi Venus encroached on Saturn.
translations.idiomatic: On a guiwei day in the twelfth month of Guangxi 1 Venus crossed Saturn.

translations.literal: The prognostication reads: "There will be internal warfare and a great battle."
translations.idiomatic: The omen read: "Civil war and a great battle."

sentences.zh: 」是後河間王為東海王越所殺。

translations.literal: Afterward the Prince of Hejian was killed by the Prince of Donghai, Yue.
translations.idiomatic: Thereafter the Prince of Hejian was killed by the Prince of Donghai, Sima Yue.

sentences.zh: 明年正月，東海王越殺諸葛玫等。

translations.literal: In the first month of the next year the Prince of Donghai, Yue, killed Zhuge Mei and others.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of the following year the Prince of Donghai, Sima Yue, put Zhuge Mei and others to death.

sentences.zh: 五月，汲桑破馮嵩，殺東燕王。

translations.literal: In the fifth month Ji Sang defeated Feng Song and killed the Prince of Dongyan.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month Ji Sang routed Feng Song and killed the Prince of Dongyan.

translations.literal: In the eighth month Gou Xi inflicted a great defeat on Ji Sang.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month Gou Xi crushed Ji Sang.

sentences.zh: 光熙元年十二月甲申，有白氣若虹，中天北下至地，夜見五日乃滅。

translations.literal: On jiashen day in the twelfth month of the first year of Guangxi there was white vapor like a rainbow, from the zenith northward down to the ground; it was visible at night for five days before vanishing.
translations.idiomatic: On a jiashen day in the twelfth month of Guangxi 1 white vapor like a rainbow stretched from the meridian northward to the ground; it shone by night for five days before fading.

translations.literal: The prognostication reads: "Great armies will rise."
translations.idiomatic: The omen read: "War will erupt on a great scale."

sentences.zh: 」明年，王彌起青、徐，汲桑亂河北，毒流天下。

translations.literal: The next year Wang Mi rose in Qing and Xu; Ji Sang stirred rebellion in Hebei; poison spread throughout the realm.
translations.idiomatic: The following year Wang Mi raised rebellion in Qing and Xu; Ji Sang ravaged Hebei; devastation spread across the empire.

sentences.zh: 孝懷帝永嘉元年九月辛亥，有大星自西南流于東北，小者如升相隨，天盡赤，聲如雷。

translations.literal: On xinhai day in the ninth month of the first year of Yongjia of Emperor Huai of Jin, a great star flowed from the southwest toward the northeast; smaller ones about the size of a sheng measure followed along; the sky turned entirely red, and there was a sound like thunder.
translations.idiomatic: On an xinhai day in the ninth month of Yongjia 1, during the reign of Emperor Huai of Jin, a great star streaked from southwest to northeast, with smaller fragments about the size of a sheng measure trailing behind; the sky turned blood-red, and thunder rolled.

translations.literal: The prognostication reads: "Shooting stars are noble envoys."
translations.idiomatic: The omen read: "Meteors signify emissaries of the great."

sentences.zh: 」是年五月，汲桑殺東燕王騰，遂據河北。

translations.literal: That year in the fifth month Ji Sang killed the Prince of Dongyan, Teng, and then occupied Hebei.
translations.idiomatic: That same year, in the fifth month, Ji Sang killed the Prince of Dongyan, Sima Teng, and seized control of Hebei.

sentences.zh: 十一月，始遣和郁為征北將軍鎮鄴，而田甄等大破汲桑，斬于樂陵。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month He Yu was first dispatched as General Who Conquers the North to garrison Ye; meanwhile Tian Zhen and others inflicted a great defeat on Ji Sang and beheaded him at Leling.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month the court at last sent He Yu as General Who Conquers the North to hold Ye; Tian Zhen and others meanwhile routed Ji Sang and executed him at Leling.

sentences.zh: 於是以甄為汲郡太守，弟蘭鉅鹿太守。

translations.literal: Thereupon Zhen was made Administrator of Ji Commandery and his younger brother Lan Administrator of Julu.
translations.idiomatic: Zhen was appointed Administrator of Ji Commandery, and his younger brother Lan was made Administrator of Julu.

sentences.zh: 小星相隨，小將別帥之象也。

translations.literal: Small stars following along—this is an image of junior generals and separate commanders.
translations.idiomatic: The trailing lesser stars were an omen of subordinate officers and regional warlords.

sentences.zh: 司馬越忿魏郡以東，平原以南，皆黨於桑，悉以賞甄等，於是侵略赤地，有聲如雷，怒之象也。

translations.literal: Sima Yue, angry that east of Wei Commandery and south of Pingyuan all had sided with Sang, rewarded Zhen and the others with those lands entirely; thereupon they invaded until the land was bare; there was a sound like thunder—an image of wrath.
translations.idiomatic: Enraged that the territories east of Wei Commandery and south of Pingyuan had all rallied to Ji Sang, Sima Yue granted those lands entirely to Tian Zhen and his allies; they then ravaged the countryside to scorched earth, and thunder rolled—omens of heaven's wrath fulfilled.

sentences.zh: 永嘉元年十二月丁亥，星流震散。

translations.literal: On dinghai day in the twelfth month of the first year of Yongjia, stars flowed and scattered in shock.
translations.idiomatic: On a dinghai day in the twelfth month of Yongjia 1, stars streaked across the sky and burst apart.

sentences.zh: 案劉向說：「天官列宿，在位之象，小星無名者，庶民之類。

translations.literal: According to Liu Xiang's interpretation: "The celestial offices and the arrayed lodges are images of those in office; nameless small stars belong to the common people.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Xiang explained the omen thus: "The starry hosts and their constellations mirror those who hold office; the innumerable lesser stars without names represent the common folk.

sentences.zh: 此百官庶民將流散之象也。

translations.literal: This is an image of the hundred officials and the myriad people about to scatter and disperse.
translations.idiomatic: This was an omen of officials and commoners about to be driven into exile and dispersal.

sentences.zh: 」是後天下大亂，百官萬民，流移轉死矣。

translations.literal: Afterward the realm fell into great disorder; the hundred officials and the myriad people drifted away, moved about, and died in turn.
translations.idiomatic: Thereafter the empire collapsed into chaos; officials and people alike were uprooted, cast about, and perished.

sentences.zh: 永嘉二年正月庚午，太白伏不見。

translations.literal: On gengwu day in the first month of the second year of Yongjia, Venus concealed itself and was not seen.
translations.idiomatic: On a gengwu day in the first month of Yongjia 2, Venus set invisibly and vanished from sight.

translations.literal: On gengzi day in the second month it first appeared at dawn in the east.
translations.idiomatic: On a gengzi day in the second month it first dawned visible in the east.

sentences.zh: 是謂當見不見，占同上條。

translations.literal: This is called "should appear but does not appear"; the prognostication is the same as the previous entry.
translations.idiomatic: This is what is meant by "due to appear yet failing to appear"; the omen is read as in the preceding passage.

sentences.zh: 其後破軍殺將，不可勝數。

translations.literal: Afterward armies were broken and generals killed beyond counting.
translations.idiomatic: Thereafter armies were shattered and commanders slain beyond number.

translations.literal: The emperor died in the barbarian court; the Central Plain was overrun and toppled.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor perished in captivity among the barbarians, and the heartland of China fell.

sentences.zh: 永嘉三年正月庚子，熒惑犯紫微。

translations.literal: On gengzi day in the first month of the third year of Yongjia, Mars encroached on the Purple Forbidden Enclosure.
translations.idiomatic: On a gengzi day in the first month of Yongjia 3, Mars crossed the Purple Forbidden Enclosure.

translations.literal: The prognostication reads: "There will be a king who dies in the wilds."
translations.idiomatic: The omen read: "A ruler will die far from his capital."

translations.literal: It also signifies fire burning the palace.
translations.idiomatic: It also portended fire consuming the palace.

sentences.zh: 」是時太史令高堂沖奏，乘輿宜遷幸，不然必無洛陽。

translations.literal: At that time the Director of Astronomy Gao Tangchong memorialized that the imperial carriage ought to move to a secondary capital; otherwise Luoyang would surely be lost.
translations.idiomatic: At that time the Director of Astronomy Gao Tangchong urged that the emperor ought to relocate the court; otherwise Luoyang would not survive.

sentences.zh: 五年六月，劉曜、王彌入京都，燒宮廟，帝崩于平陽。

translations.literal: In the sixth month of the fifth year Liu Yao and Wang Mi entered the capital, burned the palaces and temples, and the emperor died at Pingyang.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month of Yongjia 5, Liu Yao and Wang Mi stormed the capital, burned the palaces and temples, and the emperor died at Pingyang.

sentences.zh: 永嘉三年，鎮星久守南斗。

translations.literal: In the third year of Yongjia Saturn long stationed at the Southern Dipper.
translations.idiomatic: In Yongjia 3 Saturn lingered for an extended period at the Southern Dipper.

sentences.zh: 占曰：「鎮星所居者，其國有福。

translations.literal: The prognostication reads: "Wherever Saturn dwells, that state will have fortune."
translations.idiomatic: The omen read: "The region where Saturn holds station will know blessing."

translations.literal: At that time the Prince of Langya, Protector over the East, first came to hold the lands of Yang.
translations.idiomatic: At that time the Prince of Langya in his role as Protector of the East first gained control of the Yang region.

sentences.zh: 其年十一月，地動，陳卓以為是地動應也。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month of that year there was an earthquake; Chen Zhuo held that this was the fulfillment of the earthquake omen.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month of that year the earth quaked; Chen Zhuo considered this the earthly fulfillment of the omen.

sentences.zh: 永嘉三年十二月乙亥，有白氣如帶出南北方各二，起地至天，貫參伐。

translations.literal: On yihai day in the twelfth month of the third year of Yongjia, there was white vapor like belts emerging north and south two each, rising from the ground to heaven, piercing Shen and Kakka.
translations.idiomatic: On a yihai day in the twelfth month of Yongjia 3, white vapor like sashes appeared—two bands each in the south and north—rising from earth to sky and cutting through Shen and Kakka.

translations.literal: The prognostication reads: "Great armies will rise throughout the realm."
translations.idiomatic: The omen read: "War will erupt on a vast scale across the empire."

sentences.zh: 」四年三月，司馬越收繆胤、繆播等；

translations.literal: In the third month of the fourth year Sima Yue arrested Miao Yin, Miao Bo, and others;
translations.idiomatic: In the third month of the fourth year Sima Yue arrested Miao Yin, Miao Bo, and others;

translations.literal: moreover turmoil spread on three fronts, and attacks and battles did not cease.
translations.idiomatic: while on three fronts armies churned like storm clouds and fighting never ceased.

sentences.zh: 五年三月，司馬越死於甯平城，石勒攻破其眾，死者十餘萬人。

translations.literal: In the third month of the fifth year Sima Yue died at Ningping; Shi Le broke through his forces, and more than a hundred thousand died.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month of the fifth year Sima Yue died at Ningping; Shi Le shattered his army, and over a hundred thousand perished.

sentences.zh: 六月，京都焚滅，帝劫虜庭。

translations.literal: In the sixth month the capital was burned and destroyed; the emperor was seized in the barbarian court.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month the capital burned; the emperor was taken captive to the barbarian lands.

sentences.zh: 永嘉五年十月，熒惑守心。

translations.literal: In the tenth month of the fifth year of Yongjia Mars stationed at the Heart.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month of Yongjia 5 Mars lingered at Antares in the Heart asterism.

translations.literal: Two years later the emperor died in the barbarian court.
translations.idiomatic: Two years later the emperor died in captivity among the barbarians.

sentences.zh: 永嘉六年七月，熒惑、歲星、鎮星、太白聚牛女之間，裴回進退。

translations.literal: In the seventh month of the sixth year of Yongjia Mars, Jupiter, Saturn, and Venus gathered between the Ox and the Girl, wavering forward and back.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month of Yongjia 6 Mars, Jupiter, Saturn, and Venus converged between the Ox and the Girl asterisms, shifting and lingering in their courses.

translations.literal: According to the prognostication: "The Ox is the allotment of Yang Province."
translations.idiomatic: The omen was read thus: "The Ox is the celestial correlate of Yang Province."

sentences.zh: 」是後兩都傾覆，而元帝中興揚土，是其應也。

translations.literal: Afterward both capitals toppled, yet Emperor Yuan revived the Yang lands—this was its fulfillment.
translations.idiomatic: Thereafter both capitals fell, yet Emperor Yuan restored order in the Yang region—the omen was fulfilled.

sentences.zh: 愍帝建武元年五月癸未，太白熒惑合於東井。

translations.literal: On guiwei day in the fifth month of the first year of Jianwu of Emperor Min Venus and Mars conjoined at the Eastern Well.
translations.idiomatic: On a guiwei day in the fifth month of Jianwu 1, during the reign of Emperor Min of Jin, Venus and Mars merged in the Eastern Well asterism.

translations.literal: The prognostication reads: "When Metal and Fire conjoin it is called 'spark'; this signifies mourning."
translations.idiomatic: The omen read: "When Venus and Mars meet it is called a 'spark'—a portent of death and mourning."

sentences.zh: 」是時帝雖劫于平陽，天下猶未敢居其虛位，災在帝也。

translations.literal: At that time although the emperor was seized at Pingyang, the realm still dared not occupy his vacant throne; the calamity fell upon the emperor himself.
translations.idiomatic: Though the emperor was already held at Pingyang, no one yet dared claim the vacant throne—the disaster was meant for the emperor alone.

translations.literal: On dingmao day in the sixth month Venus encroached on Taiwei.
translations.idiomatic: On a dingmao day in the sixth month Venus crossed the Supreme Palace Enclosure.

sentences.zh: 占曰：「兵入天子廷，王者惡之。

translations.literal: The prognostication reads: "When armies enter the Son of Heaven's court, rulers find it ominous."
translations.idiomatic: The omen read: "Arms in the imperial court—rulers dread this sign."

sentences.zh: 」七月，愍帝崩于寇庭，天下行服大臨。

translations.literal: In the seventh month Emperor Min died in the invaders' court; throughout the realm mourning garments were worn in the great mourning rites.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month Emperor Min died in enemy hands; the empire donned mourning garb for the state funeral.

sentences.zh: 晉元帝太興元年七月，太白犯南斗。

translations.literal: In the seventh month of the first year of Taixing of Emperor Yuan of Jin Venus encroached on the Southern Dipper.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month of Taixing 1, during the reign of Emperor Yuan of Jin, Venus crossed the Southern Dipper.

translations.literal: The prognostication reads: "Wu and Yue will suffer warfare; great men will be troubled."
translations.idiomatic: The omen read: "War will come to Wu and Yue; the mighty will grieve."

translations.literal: On jiashen day in the second month of the second year Mars encroached on the Eastern Well.
translations.idiomatic: On a jiashen day in the second year Mars crossed the Eastern Well asterism.

translations.literal: The prognostication reads: "Armies will rise; nobles will slay one another."
translations.idiomatic: The omen read: "War will break out and the great will turn on one another."

translations.literal: On jimao day in the eighth month Venus encroached on the great star of Xuanyuan.
translations.idiomatic: On a jimao day in the eighth month Venus crossed the chief star of Xuanyuan.

translations.literal: The prognostication reads: "The inner palace will suffer anxiety."
translations.idiomatic: The omen read: "The harem will know sorrow."

translations.literal: On yiwei day Venus encroached on Jupiter, in the Wings.
translations.idiomatic: On a yiwei day Venus crossed Jupiter in the Wings asterism.

translations.literal: The prognostication reads: "This signifies military disorder."
translations.idiomatic: The omen read: "War and rebellion."

sentences.zh: 」三年四月壬辰，枉矢出虛、危，沒翼、軫。

translations.literal: On renchen day in the fourth month of the third year a Crooked Arrow star issued from Emptiness and Rooftop and set at the Wings and Chariot Pivot.
translations.idiomatic: On a renchen day in the fourth year a Crooked Arrow comet rose from Emptiness and Rooftop and vanished in the Wings and Chariot Pivot.

sentences.zh: 占曰：「枉矢所觸，天下之所伐。

translations.literal: The prognostication reads: "Where the Crooked Arrow touches, that is what the realm will attack."
translations.idiomatic: The omen read: "The region the Crooked Arrow strikes is the one the empire will march against."

translations.literal: The Wings and Chariot Pivot are the allotment of Jing Province.
translations.idiomatic: The Wings and Chariot Pivot are the celestial correlates of Jing Province.

sentences.zh: 」五月戊子，太白入太微，又犯上將。

translations.literal: On wuzi day in the fifth month Venus entered Taiwei and again encroached on the Upper General.
translations.idiomatic: On a wuzi day in the fifth month Venus entered the Supreme Palace Enclosure and crossed the Upper General star.

translations.literal: The prognostication reads: "The Son of Heaven will lead in person; the upper general will be executed."
translations.idiomatic: The omen read: "The emperor will take the field himself—and a supreme commander will be put to death."

sentences.zh: 」六月丙辰，太白與歲星合于房。

translations.literal: On bingchen day in the sixth month Venus and Jupiter conjoined in the Room.
translations.idiomatic: On a bingchen day in the sixth month Venus and Jupiter merged in the Room asterism.

translations.literal: The prognostication reads: "This signifies war and famine."
translations.idiomatic: The omen read: "War and famine."

translations.literal: In the ninth month Venus encroached on the Southern Dipper; the prognostication matches the first year.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month Venus crossed the Southern Dipper; the reading matched that of the first year.

sentences.zh: 十月己亥，熒惑在東井，居五諸侯南，踟蹰留止，積三十日。

translations.literal: On jihai day in the tenth month Mars was in the Eastern Well, south of the Five Feudal Lords, halting and lingering in hesitation for thirty days in all.
translations.idiomatic: On a jihai day in the tenth month Mars stood in the Eastern Well, south of the Five Feudal Lords, wavering in place for a full thirty days.

sentences.zh: 占曰：「熒惑守井二十日以上，大人憂；

translations.literal: The prognostication reads: "When Mars stations at the Well for more than twenty days, great men will be troubled;
translations.idiomatic: The omen read: "Mars lingering at the Well for more than twenty days brings grief to the mighty;

translations.literal: when it stations at the Five Feudal Lords, among the feudal lords there will be those executed.
translations.idiomatic: when it holds at the Five Feudal Lords, some among the feudal lords will be put to death.

translations.literal: On jiwei day in the twelfth month Venus entered the moon, in the Dipper.
translations.idiomatic: On a jiwei day in the twelfth month Venus entered the moon in the Dipper asterism.

sentences.zh: 郭景純曰：「月屬坎，陰府法象也。

translations.literal: Guo Jingchun said: "The moon belongs to Kan—the yin treasury and its emblem of law.
translations.idiomatic: Guo Jingchun said: "The moon corresponds to Kan, the yin domain and the celestial emblem of justice.

sentences.zh: 太白金行而來犯之，天意若曰刑理失中，自毀其法也。

translations.literal: Venus, the Metal element, came to encroach upon it—Heaven's intent seemed to say that penal justice had lost its balance and destroyed its own law.
translations.idiomatic: Venus, agent of the Metal element, came to cross it—Heaven seemed to declare that justice had lost its center and the law was undoing itself.

sentences.zh: 」四年十二月丁亥，月犯歲星在房。

translations.literal: On dinghai day in the twelfth month of the fourth year the moon encroached on Jupiter in the Room.
translations.idiomatic: On a dinghai day in the twelfth month of the fourth year the moon crossed Jupiter in the Room asterism.

translations.literal: The prognostication reads: "That state will suffer war and famine; the people will flee in exile."
translations.idiomatic: The omen read: "War and famine will afflict the realm; the people will be driven into exile."

sentences.zh: 」永昌元年三月，王敦率江、荊之眾，來攻京都，六軍距戰，敗績。

translations.literal: In the third month of the first year of Yongchang Wang Dun led the armies of Jiang and Jing to attack the capital; the Six Armies resisted in battle and suffered defeat.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month of Yongchang 1 Wang Dun marched the armies of Jiang and Jing against the capital; the imperial forces met him in battle and were routed.

sentences.zh: 於是殺護軍將軍周顗、尚書令刁協，驃騎將軍劉隗出奔。

translations.literal: Thereupon the Protector-General Zhou Yi and the Director of the Masters of Writing Diao Xie were killed; the Rapid Cavalry General Liu Wei fled.
translations.idiomatic: Zhou Yi, Protector-General, and Diao Xie, Director of the Masters of Writing, were executed; Liu Wei, Rapid Cavalry General, fled.

sentences.zh: 四月，又殺湘州刺史譙王承、鎮南將軍甘卓。

translations.literal: In the fourth month the Inspector of Xiang Province, Prince Qiao Cheng, and the General Who Guards the South Gan Zhuo were also killed.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month Prince Qiao Cheng, Inspector of Xiang, and Gan Zhuo, General Who Guards the South, were also slain.

translations.literal: In the intercalary twelfth month Emperor Yuan died.
translations.idiomatic: In the intercalary twelfth month Emperor Yuan died.

sentences.zh: 間一年，敦亦梟夷，枉矢觸翼之應也。

translations.literal: A year later Dun too was executed and his clan exterminated—the fulfillment of the Crooked Arrow touching the Wings.
translations.idiomatic: Within a year Wang Dun too was executed and his line extinguished—the fulfillment of the Crooked Arrow's strike on the Wings.

sentences.zh: 十月，石他入豫州，略城父、銍二縣民以北，刺史祖約遣軍追之，為其所沒，遂退守壽春。

translations.literal: In the tenth month Shi Ta entered Yuzhou, carried off the people of Chengfü and Zhi counties northward; the Inspector Zu Yue sent troops in pursuit and was destroyed by him; he then withdrew to defend Shouchun.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month Shi Ta invaded Yuzhou and drove the people of Chengfü and Zhi north; Inspector Zu Yue sent troops in pursuit, only to be wiped out; Zu then fell back to defend Shouchun.

sentences.zh: 明帝太寧三年正月，熒惑逆行入太微。

translations.literal: In the first month of the third year of Taining of Emperor Ming Mars moved retrograde and entered Taiwei.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of Taining 3, during the reign of Emperor Ming, Mars turned retrograde and entered the Supreme Palace Enclosure.

translations.literal: The prognostication reads: "This portends war and mourning; rulers find it ominous."
translations.idiomatic: The omen read: "War and death—and rulers dread it."

translations.literal: In the intercalary eighth month the emperor died.
translations.idiomatic: In the intercalary eighth month the emperor died.

sentences.zh: 咸和二年，蘇峻反，攻宮室，太后以憂逼崩，天子幽劫于石頭，遠近兵亂，至四年乃息。

translations.literal: In the second year of Xianhe Su Jun rebelled and attacked the palace halls; the Empress Dowager died from grief and distress; the Son of Heaven was seized and held at Shitou; near and far armies fell into disorder, which did not cease until the fourth year.
translations.idiomatic: In Xianhe 2 Su Jun rebelled and stormed the palace; the Empress Dowager died of grief; the emperor was taken captive at Shitou; war engulfed the region and did not subside until the fourth year.

sentences.zh: 成帝咸和四年七月，有星孛于西北，二十三日滅。

translations.literal: In the seventh month of the fourth year of Xianhe of Emperor Cheng a broom star appeared in the northwest and vanished after twenty-three days.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month of Xianhe 4, during the reign of Emperor Cheng, a comet blazed in the northwest and faded after twenty-three days.

translations.literal: The prognostication reads: "This signifies military disorder."
translations.idiomatic: The omen read: "War and rebellion."

sentences.zh: 」十二月，郭默殺江州刺史劉胤，荊州刺史陶侃討默，明年，斬之。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month Guo Mo killed the Inspector of Jiang Province Liu Yin; the Inspector of Jing Province Tao Kan campaigned against Mo; the next year he was beheaded.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month Guo Mo murdered Liu Yin, Inspector of Jiang; Tao Kan, Inspector of Jing, marched against him and beheaded him the following year.

translations.literal: At that time Shi Le also first assumed a usurped title.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Shi Le also first declared himself emperor in usurpation.

sentences.zh: 咸和六年正月丙辰，月入南斗。

translations.literal: On bingchen day in the first month of the sixth year of Xianhe the moon entered the Southern Dipper.
translations.idiomatic: On a bingchen day in the first month of Xianhe 6 the moon entered the Southern Dipper.

translations.literal: The prognostication reads: "There will be warfare."
translations.idiomatic: The omen read: "War."

translations.literal: One interpretation reads: "There will be a great amnesty."
translations.idiomatic: Another reading held: "A great amnesty."

sentences.zh: 」是月胡賊殺略婁、武進二縣民，於是遣戍中洲。

translations.literal: That month barbarian raiders killed and plundered the people of Lou and Wujin counties; thereupon garrisons were dispatched to Zhongzhou.
translations.idiomatic: That month foreign raiders slaughtered and pillaged the people of Lou and Wujin; the court then sent troops to garrison Zhongzhou.

sentences.zh: 明年，胡賊又略南沙、海虞民。

translations.literal: The next year barbarian raiders again plundered the people of Nansha and Haiyu.
translations.idiomatic: The following year the raiders again ravaged the people of Nansha and Haiyu.

sentences.zh: 是年正月，大赦，伐淮南，討襄陽，平之。

translations.literal: In the first month of that year there was a great amnesty; they campaigned against Huainan, subjugated Xiangyang, and pacified it.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of that year a great amnesty was proclaimed; the court campaigned in Huainan, attacked Xiangyang, and pacified it.

sentences.zh: 咸和六年十一月，熒惑守胃、昴。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month of the sixth year of Xianhe Mars stationed at the Stomach and the Hairy Head.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month of Xianhe 6 Mars lingered in the Stomach and Hairy Head asterisms.

translations.literal: The prognostication reads: "Zhao and Wei will suffer warfare."
translations.idiomatic: The omen read: "War will come to Zhao and Wei."

sentences.zh: 」八年七月，石勒死，石虎自立，多所殘滅。

translations.literal: In the seventh month of the eighth year Shi Le died; Shi Hu installed himself and slaughtered many.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year Shi Le died; Shi Hu seized power and massacred on a vast scale.

sentences.zh: 是時雖勒、虎僭號，而其強弱常占於昴，不關太微紫宮也。

translations.literal: Although at that time Le and Hu usurped titles, their strength and weakness were regularly read from the Hairy Head and did not concern the Purple Forbidden Enclosure of Taiwei.
translations.idiomatic: Though Le and Hu had declared themselves emperors, their fortunes were read from the Hairy Head asterism, not from the Purple Forbidden Enclosure or the Supreme Palace.

sentences.zh: 咸和八年三月己巳，月入南斗，與六年占同。

translations.literal: On jisi day in the third month of the eighth year of Xianhe the moon entered the Southern Dipper; the prognostication matches the sixth year.
translations.idiomatic: On a jisi day in the third month of Xianhe 8 the moon entered the Southern Dipper; the reading matched that of the sixth year.

sentences.zh: 其年七月，石勒死，彭彪以譙，石生以長安，郭權以秦州，並歸從。

translations.literal: In the seventh month of that year Shi Le died; Peng Biao held Qiao, Shi Sheng held Chang'an, and Guo Quan held Qin Province—all submitting and following.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month of that year Shi Le died; Peng Biao held Qiao, Shi Sheng held Chang'an, and Guo Quan held Qin Province—all rallying in allegiance.

sentences.zh: 於是遣督護高球率眾救彪，彪敗球退。

translations.literal: Thereupon the Supervisor-General Gao Qiu was dispatched leading troops to rescue Biao; Biao was defeated and Qiu withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: The court sent Supervisor-General Gao Qiu with an army to relieve Peng Biao; Biao was defeated and Qiu retreated.

translations.literal: Moreover Shi Hu and Shi Bin attacked and destroyed Sheng and Quan.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Hu and Shi Bin then attacked and destroyed Shi Sheng and Guo Quan.

translations.literal: In the first month of the first year of Xiankang there was a great amnesty.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of Xiankang 1 a great amnesty was proclaimed.

sentences.zh: 咸和八年七月，熒惑入昴。

translations.literal: In the seventh month of the eighth year of Xianhe Mars entered the Hairy Head.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month of Xianhe 8 Mars entered the Hairy Head asterism.

translations.literal: The prognostication reads: "The barbarian king will die."
translations.idiomatic: The omen read: "A barbarian king will die."

translations.literal: Shi Hu attacked and destroyed many.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Hu attacked and destroyed on a vast scale.

translations.literal: In the eighth month the moon encroached on the Hairy Head.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month the moon crossed the Hairy Head asterism.

translations.literal: The prognostication reads: "The barbarians will not be at peace."
translations.idiomatic: The omen read: "The barbarian lands will know unrest."

translations.literal: In the sixth month of the ninth year the moon again encroached on the Hairy Head.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month of the ninth year the moon crossed the Hairy Head again.

sentences.zh: 是時石弘雖襲勒位，而石虎擅威暴橫。

translations.literal: At that time although Shi Hong had inherited Le's throne, Shi Hu wielded power in a tyrannical and violent fashion.
translations.idiomatic: Though Shi Hong had succeeded to Le's throne, Shi Hu held real power and ruled with brutal arrogance.

sentences.zh: 十月，廢弘自立，遂幽殺之。

translations.literal: In the tenth month he deposed Hong and installed himself, then secretly executed him.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month he deposed Hong, seized the throne himself, and had him murdered in confinement.

sentences.zh: 咸和九年三月己亥，熒惑入輿鬼，犯積屍。

translations.literal: On jihai day in the third month of the ninth year of Xianhe Mars entered the Carriage Ghost and encroached on Accumulated Corpses.
translations.idiomatic: On a jihai day in the third month of Xianhe 9 Mars entered the Carriage Ghost asterism and trespassed against Accumulated Corpses.

sentences.zh: 占曰：「兵在西北，有沒軍死將。

translations.literal: The prognostication reads: "War lies in the northwest; an army will be destroyed and a general will die."
translations.idiomatic: The omen read: "War will come to the northwest—an army will be lost and a general will perish."

sentences.zh: 」四月，鎮西將軍、雍州刺史郭權始以秦州歸從，尋為石斌所滅，徙其眾於青、徐。

translations.literal: In the fourth month the Defender-General of the West and Governor of Yong Province Guo Quan first submitted Qin Province in allegiance; soon he was destroyed by Shi Bin, and his followers were relocated to Qing and Xu.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month Guo Quan, Defender-General of the West and Governor of Yong, first submitted Qin Province in allegiance; before long Shi Bin destroyed him and resettled his followers in Qing and Xu.

sentences.zh: 晉成帝咸康元年二月己亥，太白犯昴。

translations.literal: On jihai day in the second month of the first year of Xiankang under Emperor Cheng of Jin Venus encroached on the Hairy Head.
translations.idiomatic: On a jihai day in the second month of Xiankang 1, during the reign of Emperor Cheng of Jin, Venus trespassed against the Hairy Head asterism.

translations.literal: The prognostication reads: "War will arise; the year will bring great drought."
translations.idiomatic: The omen read: "War will break out, and the year will bring severe drought."

translations.literal: In the fourth month Shi Hu's raiding cavalry reached Liyang.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month Shi Hu's mounted raiders reached Liyang.

sentences.zh: 朝廷慮其眾也，加司徒王導大司馬，治兵動眾。

translations.literal: The court, concerned at their numbers, additionally appointed Minister over the Masses Wang Dao Grand Marshal and mobilized troops.
translations.idiomatic: Alarmed by the size of the force, the court named Wang Dao, Minister over the Masses, Grand Marshal as well and mustered an army.

sentences.zh: 又遣慈湖、牛渚、蕪湖三戍。

translations.literal: It also dispatched garrisons at Cihu, Niuzhu, and Wuhu.
translations.idiomatic: Three garrisons were also posted at Cihu, Niuzhu, and Wuhu.
